name: Whey glycoproteins
description: Whey glycoproteins (CAS 84082-51-9 ), also referenced commercially as glycoproteins, bovine-whey, are a class of bioactive proteins derived from bovine milk whey. They carry carbohydrate chains that enhance their functional stability in complex formulations. They serve as antioxidants and stabilizers across food, pharmaceutical, and biotechnological applications where protein-carbohydrate conjugates offer performance advantages over conventional proteins. These properties make them highly versatile for industrial use. In functional food and sports nutrition products, whey glycoproteins contribute antioxidant activity and help stabilize emulsions and protein matrices during processing and shelf life. This ensures a consistent texture and quality for the end consumer. Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate them into nutraceutical capsules and bioactive delivery systems where controlled protein stability is critical to product efficacy. They are essential for maintaining the integrity of sensitive active ingredients. In biotechnology, they are used as reference materials and functional components in cell culture media and assay development. Animal feed manufacturers apply them in premium feed supplements targeting immune support and gut health. Whey glycoproteins are typically supplied as a lyophilized powder or spray-dried powder, suited for both laboratory-scale and industrial formulation. Standard grades include food-grade and research-grade specifications for various needs. Some suppliers offer material aligned to USP protein reference standards to ensure the highest quality.
